# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

CMJ Fatigue Traffic Light — a post-practice neuromuscular fatigue monitoring tool for Baylor Volleyball. It ingests ForceDecks countermovement jump (CMJ) CSV exports, pairs pre/post-practice tests per athlete, computes percent change on 6 biomechanical metrics, assigns traffic-light colors (green/yellow/red), and renders a self-contained HTML report. A separate recovery monitoring report tracks pre-practice CMJ trends across sessions to detect inter-session fatigue accumulation.

## Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Full pipeline (import CSVs + generate fatigue report for today)
python scripts/run_pipeline.py

# Full pipeline with overrides
python scripts/run_pipeline.py --date 2026-03-03 --session "Pre-Practice Assessment"

# Step-by-step (manual fallback)
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --date 2026-07-06
python scripts/generate_report.py --date 2026-07-06

# Hawkin ingest options
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py                       # last 14 days
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --all                 # entire account history
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --probe               # print raw API fields, write nothing
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --dry-run             # show what would be written

# Legacy CSV import (only if hand-importing a ForceDecks export)
python scripts/import_data.py

# Recovery monitoring report (last 6 sessions up to today)
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py

# Recovery report with overrides
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py --date 2026-03-20 --sessions 4
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py --output output/custom.html

# Run all tests
python -m pytest tests/ -v

# Run a single test file
python -m pytest tests/test_thresholds.py -v

# Send a specific past report manually
python scripts/send_email.py --date 2026-04-10
```

The `run_report.bat` in the project root wraps `run_pipeline.py` for non-technical staff use (double-click to run). It imports CSVs, generates the report, opens it in the browser, and emails it to recipients in `email_config.yaml`.
`run_recovery_report.bat` wraps `generate_recovery_report.py` for non-technical staff use (double-click to run).

## Architecture

### Data Flow

```
Hawkin Dynamics API → fetch_hawkin.py ─┐
                                       ├→ data/master_data.csv → generate_report.py → output/report_YYYY-MM-DD.html
ForceDecks CSV → import_data.py ───────┘                       → generate_recovery_report.py → output/recovery_report_YYYY-MM-DD.html
```

**The Hawkin API is the live data source as of 2026-07-22.** `import_data.py` is retained for hand-importing a ForceDecks CSV but is no longer part of the normal pipeline. See `docs/HAWKIN_API_INTEGRATION.md`.

`run_pipeline.py` chains fetch + fatigue report in a single invocation and auto-opens the report in the browser. The recovery report is run separately.

### Key Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config/config.yaml` | Single source of truth: column mapping, pre/post pairing method, per-metric thresholds, roster, recommendations, legend text |
| `scripts/utils.py` | Pure threshold logic (`calc_pct_change`, `get_metric_color`, `assign_overall_color`, `build_roster_map`) — imported by both report scripts and tests |
| `scripts/fetch_hawkin.py` | **Primary ingest.** Pulls CMJ trials from the Hawkin API → `master_data.csv`. Deduplicates on Hawkin trial id, so re-running any date range is safe. `--probe` prints raw API fields |
| `scripts/import_data.py` | Legacy ForceDecks CSV importer. Retained for manual use; not in the normal pipeline |
| `scripts/generate_report.py` | Reads `master_data.csv`, pairs pre/post, computes metrics, renders Jinja2 HTML fatigue report |
| `scripts/generate_recovery_report.py` | Reads `master_data.csv`, builds pre-session trend grids across N sessions, assigns recovery badges, renders Jinja2 HTML recovery report |
| `scripts/run_pipeline.py` | Orchestrates import + fatigue report in one call; prints `REPORT_PATH=...` on success for downstream use |
| `scripts/send_email.py` | Sends a report via Outlook COM automation; accepts a path arg or `--date YYYY-MM-DD`; reads recipients/subject/body from `email_config.yaml` |
| `config/email_config.yaml` | Email recipients, subject template (`{date}` is replaced with the report date), and body text |
| `templates/report_template.html` | Jinja2 template for daily fatigue report; fully self-contained HTML (works offline) |
| `templates/recovery_report_template.html` | Jinja2 template for recovery monitoring report; fully self-contained HTML (works offline) |
| `data/master_data.csv` | Cumulative test history; auto-created on first import |

### Metric Scoring Logic (`utils.py`)

- **Per-metric color**: percent change from pre → post compared against `yellow_min` / `red_min` thresholds in `config.yaml`. Direction is `decrease_bad` (jump height, RSI, force, RFD) or `increase_bad` (time-to-takeoff, CM depth).
- **Overall color**: green = 0–1 metrics outside green; yellow = 2–3 yellows OR 1 red; red = 2+ reds OR 3+ yellows+reds.

### Recovery Report Logic (`generate_recovery_report.py`)

Each cell in the athlete × session grid is colored by the **worst of two signals**:
- **Signal 1** — session-to-session delta: `calc_pct_change(prev_pre, current_pre)` vs config thresholds.
- **Signal 2** — deviation from personal window average: `calc_pct_change(baseline, current_pre)` vs config thresholds. Baseline = mean of athlete's non-null pre values across all sessions in the window (computed once per athlete/metric, not per cell).

Cell indicators: `↓`/`↑` = moderate deviation from window average; `↓↓`/`↑↑` = large deviation. Direction matches metric direction (`decrease_bad` → `↓`/`↓↓`; `increase_bad` → `↑`/`↑↑`).

Recovery badges per athlete across all 6 metrics × N sessions: **At Risk** (2+ red OR 3+ yellow+red) → **Watch** (2+ yellow OR 1 red) → **Recovered** (otherwise).

### Pre/Post Pairing

**Hawkin path (`fetch_hawkin.py`)** splits at the largest time gap within each athlete-date, governed by `hawkin.min_split_gap_minutes` (default 45). Neither tags nor clock windows work on this account: only 34 of 1,728 trials carry any tag and no pre-practice tag exists, and practices alternate morning (~07:30 pre / ~10:00 post) and afternoon (~14:15 pre / ~16:35 post), which fixed windows cannot separate. A genuine pre/post split shows a median gap of 131 minutes; trials within one bout are seconds apart. If no gap exceeds the threshold the session was a single bout and all trials are labelled `pre`.

Multiple trials per phase are reduced by `hawkin.trial_aggregation` (default `mean`).

**Legacy CSV path (`import_data.py`)** still uses `pairing.method` in `config.yaml` — `"tag"` (ForceDecks `Tags` column) or `"time"` (configured windows). If an athlete has multiple pre or post rows on the same date, the latest test by time is used.

### Column Mapping

`config.yaml` `column_mapping:` maps internal field names to exact ForceDecks column headers. If ForceDecks changes export headers, update only this section — no code changes needed.

### Roster

`config.yaml` `roster:` names must match ForceDecks exports exactly (spelling and capitalization). Athletes not in the roster still appear in reports but without jersey number and position.

## Known Gotchas

- **Date format in master_data.csv**: Dates are stored as `%-m/%-d/%Y` (e.g. `3/2/2026`), not ISO 8601. Use `pd.to_datetime(df["test_date"], format="mixed")` when reading — do not omit `format="mixed"` or it will fail on mixed-format columns.
- **Duplicate imports**: applies to the *legacy CSV path only*. Running `import_data.py` twice on the same CSVs appends duplicate rows. Symptom: two date-format variants for the same date in `master_data.csv`. `fetch_hawkin.py` does not have this problem — it deduplicates on Hawkin trial id.
- **Hawkin returns SI units, and countermovement depth is negative.** `Jump Height(m)` and `Countermovement Depth(m)` are metres, `Time To Takeoff(s)` is seconds. CM depth arrives as a negative number, so it is mapped with `absolute: true` — without that, the `increase_bad` direction inverts and a deeper dip reads as improvement. All handled in `config.yaml` → `hawkin.metric_mapping`.
- **The Hawkin tests endpoint is the API root**, e.g. `https://cloud.hawkindynamics.com/api/v1?from=...`. There is no `/tests` path; requesting one returns 404.
- **Thresholds are vendor-specific.** `ecc_braking_rfd` and `countermovement_depth` were recalibrated for Hawkin in July 2026 because their original ForceDecks-tuned values sat below Hawkin's measurement noise floor. Do not copy thresholds between force-plate systems without checking them against measured trial-to-trial variability — see `docs/HAWKIN_API_INTEGRATION.md` §6.

## Configuration — No Code Changes Needed For

- Adjusting green/yellow/red thresholds: edit `thresholds.*.yellow_min` / `red_min`
- Changing recommendation language: edit `recommendations.*`
- Adding/removing athletes: edit `roster:`
- Changing ForceDecks column headers: edit `column_mapping:`
# CMJ Fatigue Traffic Light
**Baylor Volleyball | Applied Performance**

Practice ends. Athletes jump. You run one command. Coaching staff has a color-coded report before the next session.

---

## Setup (one time)

### 1. Install Python dependencies

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. Update the roster

Open `config.yaml` and edit the `roster:` section so athlete names match exactly how they appear in ForceDecks.

### 3. Verify column mapping

## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

"""
run_pipeline.py -- One-command pipeline: fetch from Hawkin and generate report.

Pulls CMJ trials from the Hawkin Dynamics API into master_data.csv, then renders
the fatigue report for the most recent session that has a pre/post pair.

Usage:
    python scripts/run_pipeline.py
    python scripts/run_pipeline.py --session "Pre-Practice Assessment"
    python scripts/run_pipeline.py --date 2026-07-06   # target a specific session

Requires HD_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env. See docs/HAWKIN_API_INTEGRATION.md.

The legacy CSV importer (import_data.py) is still present and still works if you
ever need to ingest a ForceDecks export by hand.
"""

import argparse
import datetime
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# ─── Paths ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SCRIPT_DIR   = Path(__file__).parent
PROJECT_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parent

# Ensure scripts/ is on the path so sibling modules are importable
sys.path.insert(0, str(SCRIPT_DIR))

from import_data import (

@echo off
setlocal
title CMJ Traffic Light Reports - Baylor Volleyball

echo.
echo  ============================================================
echo   CMJ Traffic Light Reports - Baylor Volleyball
echo  ============================================================
echo.

:: Work from the folder this file lives in, wherever it was unzipped
cd /d "%~dp0"

set "UV=%~dp0.tools\uv.exe"
set "UVRUN=run --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements requirements.txt"

:: ── 1. Python runtime (first run only) ─────────────────────────────────────────
:: uv fetches a private Python and the packages into its own cache under
:: %LOCALAPPDATA%. Nothing is installed system-wide and no admin rights are needed.
if exist "%UV%" goto have_uv
echo  First run: downloading the Python runner (about 20 MB)...
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol='Tls12'; $z=Join-Path $env:TEMP 'cmj-uv.zip'; Invoke-WebRequest -UseBasicParsing 'https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/latest/download/uv-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip' -OutFile $z; Expand-Archive $z -DestinationPath '.tools' -Force; Remove-Item $z"
if not exist "%UV%" (
    echo.
    echo  Could not download the Python runner. Check the internet connection and try again.
    goto end
)
:have_uv

:: ── 2. Hawkin token (first run only) ───────────────────────────────────────────
if exist ".env" goto have_token
echo.
echo  First run: this needs your Hawkin Dynamics refresh token.
echo  Get it at cloud.hawkindynamics.com - Settings - Integrations.
echo.
set /p "HDTOKEN=  Paste token and press Enter: "
if not defined HDTOKEN (
    echo  No token entered. Nothing was run.
    goto end
)
:: Written through PowerShell so characters like & or > in the token survive
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Set-Content -Path '.env' -Value ('HD_REFRESH_TOKEN=' + $env:HDTOKEN.Trim()) -Encoding ascii"
echo  Token saved.
:have_token

:: ── 3. Test history (first run only) ───────────────────────────────────────────
:: The daily pull only looks back 14 days; the recovery report wants 6 sessions,
:: so the first run backfills everything. Re-runs never duplicate trials.
if exist "data\master_data.csv" goto have_history
echo.
echo  First run: downloading test history from Hawkin. This takes a few minutes...
"%UV%" %UVRUN% scripts\fetch_hawkin.py --all
if errorlevel 1 goto failed
:have_history

:: ── 4. Reports ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
echo.
"%UV%" %UVRUN% scripts\run_pipeline.py %*
if errorlevel 1 goto failed

echo.
"%UV%" %UVRUN% scripts\generate_recovery_report.py
if errorlevel 1 goto failed

echo.
echo  Reports are in: %~dp0output
start "" explorer "%~dp0output"
goto end

:failed
echo.
echo  Something went wrong - read the message above.
echo  If it mentions the token (401 or 403), delete the .env file in this folder
echo  and run again to enter a new one.

:end
echo.
pause

input.content:
CMJ Traffic Light Reports - Baylor Volleyball
Applied Performance
=============================================

Two reports from the Hawkin force plates:

  report_YYYY-MM-DD.html            Post-practice fatigue: pre vs post CMJ,
                                    green / yellow / red per athlete.
  recovery_report_YYYY-MM-DD.html   Recovery trend: pre-practice CMJ across
                                    the last 6 sessions.

Both land in the "output" folder, and open in your browser when the run ends.


BEFORE THE FIRST RUN
--------------------
1. You need a login to Baylor Volleyball's Hawkin Dynamics account.
2. In Hawkin (cloud.hawkindynamics.com), go to Settings > Integrations and
   generate a refresh token. Copy it.


EVERY RUN
---------
1. Unzip this folder somewhere on your computer (not inside the zip itself).
2. Double-click "Run CMJ Report.bat".
3. Wait for the window to say the reports are ready. Press any key to close it.

The fatigue report covers the most recent session that has both pre- and
post-practice jumps. Run it after the post-practice jumps are uploaded.


THE FIRST RUN IS SLOWER
-----------------------
The first time, the window will:
  - download a small Python runner (nothing is installed on your computer,
    no admin rights needed),
  - ask you to paste the Hawkin token (saved in this folder as ".env"),
  - download the team's full test history.
Allow a few minutes. Later runs take seconds.

If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click "More info", then "Run anyway".


IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG
-----------------------

"""
build_share_package.py -- Zip the reports into a package a colleague can run.

The package holds only what the two reports need: the Hawkin fetch, both report
generators, templates and config. It leaves out email, tests, docs, and anything
private (.env, data/, output/). The colleague double-clicks "Run CMJ Report.bat";
see share/README.txt for what they see.

Usage:
    python scripts/build_share_package.py
    python scripts/build_share_package.py --out C:/Users/me/Desktop
"""

import argparse
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT_DIR   = Path(__file__).parent
PROJECT_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parent
SHARE_DIR    = PROJECT_ROOT / "share"

PACKAGE_NAME = "CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report"

# run_pipeline imports import_data, so the legacy importer ships too.
SCRIPTS = [
    "fetch_hawkin.py",
    "generate_report.py",
    "generate_recovery_report.py",
    "run_pipeline.py",
    "import_data.py",
    "utils.py",
]

# Files cmd.exe or Notepad read; they need Windows line endings.
CRLF_SUFFIXES = {".bat", ".txt"}


def package_files() -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    """(source path, path inside the package) for every file shipped."""
    files = [(SCRIPT_DIR / name, f"scripts/{name}") for name in SCRIPTS]
    files.append((PROJECT_ROOT / "config" / "config.yaml", "config/config.yaml"))
    files += [(p, f"templates/{p.name}") for p in sorted((PROJECT_ROOT / "templates").glob("*.html"))]
    files += [(p, p.name) for p in sorted(SHARE_DIR.iterdir()) if p.is_file()]
    return files


def build(out_dir: Path) -> Path:
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    zip_path = out_dir / f"{PACKAGE_NAME}.zip"

    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        for src, arcname in package_files():
            data = src.read_bytes()
            if src.suffix.lower() in CRLF_SUFFIXES:
                data = data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n").replace(b"\n", b"\r\n")
            zf.writestr(f"{PACKAGE_NAME}/{arcname}", data)
        # Empty output folder so the colleague sees where reports will go
        zf.writestr(f"{PACKAGE_NAME}/output/", b"")

    return zip_path


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build the shareable CMJ report package")
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=PROJECT_ROOT / "dist",
                   help="Folder to write the zip into (default: dist/)")
    args = p.parse_args()

    zip_path = build(args.out)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path) as zf:
        names = zf.namelist()
    print(f"Built {zip_path} ({len(names)} entries)")
    for n in names:
        print(f"  {n}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
The launcher, README and requirements are committed and pushed to branch `worktree-share-package` on GitHub. The permission system blocked me twice from writing the zip build script, even after you cleared it, so the zip is a short manual step below.

**What I checked:** the launcher's run command builds Python 3.12 with pandas, pyyaml and jinja2, and both report scripts load in it. I couldn't run the live Hawkin pull or a full double-click run here, because this machine has no token and no data. Mike's first run is the real test.

## Steps to send it to Mike

**1. Confirm Mike has Hawkin access.** He needs his own login to Baylor Volleyball's Hawkin account, so he can generate a refresh token at cloud.hawkindynamics.com → Settings → Integrations. Without that the package can't pull any data. Don't send him your token.

**2. Build the folder** (about two minutes in File Explorer). Make a folder named `CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report` and copy these into it. The source is `Desktop\DEV\cmj-traffic-light\.claude\worktrees\share-package\`:

```
CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report\
  Run CMJ Report.bat     ← from share\
  README.txt             ← from share\
  requirements.txt       ← from share\  (NOT the root one; that one pulls in the Outlook package)
  config\config.yaml
  scripts\fetch_hawkin.py, generate_report.py, generate_recovery_report.py,
          run_pipeline.py, import_data.py, utils.py
  templates\report_template.html, recovery_report_template.html
  output\                (empty folder)
```

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

CMJ Fatigue Traffic Light — a post-practice neuromuscular fatigue monitoring tool for Baylor Volleyball. It ingests ForceDecks countermovement jump (CMJ) CSV exports, pairs pre/post-practice tests per athlete, computes percent change on 6 biomechanical metrics, assigns traffic-light colors (green/yellow/red), and renders a self-contained HTML report. A separate recovery monitoring report tracks pre-practice CMJ trends across sessions to detect inter-session fatigue accumulation.

## Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Full pipeline (import CSVs + generate fatigue report for today)
python scripts/run_pipeline.py

# Full pipeline with overrides
python scripts/run_pipeline.py --date 2026-03-03 --session "Pre-Practice Assessment"

# Step-by-step (manual fallback)
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --date 2026-07-06
python scripts/generate_report.py --date 2026-07-06

# Hawkin ingest options
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py                       # last 14 days
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --all                 # entire account history
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --probe               # print raw API fields, write nothing
python scripts/fetch_hawkin.py --dry-run             # show what would be written

# Legacy CSV import (only if hand-importing a ForceDecks export)
python scripts/import_data.py

# Recovery monitoring report (last 6 sessions up to today)
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py

# Recovery report with overrides
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py --date 2026-03-20 --sessions 4
python scripts/generate_recovery_report.py --output output/custom.html

# Run all tests
python -m pytest tests/ -v

# Run a single test file
python -m pytest tests/test_thresholds.py -v

# Send a specific past report manually
python scripts/send_email.py --date 2026-04-10
```

The `run_report.bat` in the project root wraps `run_pipeline.py` for non-technical staff use (double-click to run). It imports CSVs, generates the report, opens it in the browser, and emails it to recipients in `email_config.yaml`.
`run_recovery_report.bat` wraps `generate_recovery_report.py` for non-technical staff use (double-click to run).

## Architecture

### Data Flow

```
Hawkin Dynamics API → fetch_hawkin.py ─┐
                                       ├→ data/master_data.csv → generate_report.py → output/report_YYYY-MM-DD.html
ForceDecks CSV → import_data.py ───────┘                       → generate_recovery_report.py → output/recovery_report_YYYY-MM-DD.html
```

**The Hawkin API is the live data source as of 2026-07-22.** `import_data.py` is retained for hand-importing a ForceDecks CSV but is no longer part of the normal pipeline. See `docs/HAWKIN_API_INTEGRATION.md`.

`run_pipeline.py` chains fetch + fatigue report in a single invocation and auto-opens the report in the browser. The recovery report is run separately.

### Key Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `config/config.yaml` | Single source of truth: column mapping, pre/post pairing method, per-metric thresholds, roster, recommendations, legend text |
| `scripts/utils.py` | Pure threshold logic (`calc_pct_change`, `get_metric_color`, `assign_overall_color`, `build_roster_map`) — imported by both report scripts and tests |
| `scripts/fetch_hawkin.py` | **Primary ingest.** Pulls CMJ trials from the Hawkin API → `master_data.csv`. Deduplicates on Hawkin trial id, so re-running any date range is safe. `--probe` prints raw API fields |
| `scripts/import_data.py` | Legacy ForceDecks CSV importer. Retained for manual use; not in the normal pipeline |
| `scripts/generate_report.py` | Reads `master_data.csv`, pairs pre/post, computes metrics, renders Jinja2 HTML fatigue report |
| `scripts/generate_recovery_report.py` | Reads `master_data.csv`, builds pre-session trend grids across N sessions, assigns recovery badges, renders Jinja2 HTML recovery report |
| `scripts/run_pipeline.py` | Orchestrates import + fatigue report in one call; prints `REPORT_PATH=...` on success for downstream use |
| `scripts/send_email.py` | Sends a report via Outlook COM automation; accepts a path arg or `--date YYYY-MM-DD`; reads recipients/subject/body from `email_config.yaml` |
| `config/email_config.yaml` | Email recipients, subject template (`{date}` is replaced with the report date), and body text |
| `templates/report_template.html` | Jinja2 template for daily fatigue report; fully self-contained HTML (works offline) |
| `templates/recovery_report_template.html` | Jinja2 template for recovery monitoring report; fully self-contained HTML (works offline) |
| `data/master_data.csv` | Cumulative test history; auto-created on first import |

### Metric Scoring Logic (`utils.py`)

- **Per-metric color**: percent change from pre → post compared against `yellow_min` / `red_min` thresholds in `config.yaml`. Direction is `decrease_bad` (jump height, RSI, force, RFD) or `increase_bad` (time-to-takeoff, CM depth).
- **Overall color**: green = 0–1 metrics outside green; yellow = 2–3 yellows OR 1 red; red = 2+ reds OR 3+ yellows+reds.

### Recovery Report Logic (`generate_recovery_report.py`)

Each cell in the athlete × session grid is colored by the **worst of two signals**:
- **Signal 1** — session-to-session delta: `calc_pct_change(prev_pre, current_pre)` vs config thresholds.
- **Signal 2** — deviation from personal window average: `calc_pct_change(baseline, current_pre)` vs config thresholds. Baseline = mean of athlete's non-null pre values across all sessions in the window (computed once per athlete/metric, not per cell).

Cell indicators: `↓`/`↑` = moderate deviation from window average; `↓↓`/`↑↑` = large deviation. Direction matches metric direction (`decrease_bad` → `↓`/`↓↓`; `increase_bad` → `↑`/`↑↑`).

Recovery badges per athlete across all 6 metrics × N sessions: **At Risk** (2+ red OR 3+ yellow+red) → **Watch** (2+ yellow OR 1 red) → **Recovered** (otherwise).

### Pre/Post Pairing

**Hawkin path (`fetch_hawkin.py`)** splits at the largest time gap within each athlete-date, governed by `hawkin.min_split_gap_minutes` (default 45). Neither tags nor clock windows work on this account: only 34 of 1,728 trials carry any tag and no pre-practice tag exists, and practices alternate morning (~07:30 pre / ~10:00 post) and afternoon (~14:15 pre / ~16:35 post), which fixed windows cannot separate. A genuine pre/post split shows a median gap of 131 minutes; trials within one bout are seconds apart. If no gap exceeds the threshold the session was a single bout and all trials are labelled `pre`.

Multiple trials per phase are reduced by `hawkin.trial_aggregation` (default `mean`).

**Legacy CSV path (`import_data.py`)** still uses `pairing.method` in `config.yaml` — `"tag"` (ForceDecks `Tags` column) or `"time"` (configured windows). If an athlete has multiple pre or post rows on the same date, the latest test by time is used.

### Column Mapping

`config.yaml` `column_mapping:` maps internal field names to exact ForceDecks column headers. If ForceDecks changes export headers, update only this section — no code changes needed.

### Roster

`config.yaml` `roster:` names must match ForceDecks exports exactly (spelling and capitalization). Athletes not in the roster still appear in reports but without jersey number and position.

## Known Gotchas

- **Date format in master_data.csv**: Dates are stored as `%-m/%-d/%Y` (e.g. `3/2/2026`), not ISO 8601. Use `pd.to_datetime(df["test_date"], format="mixed")` when reading — do not omit `format="mixed"` or it will fail on mixed-format columns.
- **Duplicate imports**: applies to the *legacy CSV path only*. Running `import_data.py` twice on the same CSVs appends duplicate rows. Symptom: two date-format variants for the same date in `master_data.csv`. `fetch_hawkin.py` does not have this problem — it deduplicates on Hawkin trial id.
- **Hawkin returns SI units, and countermovement depth is negative.** `Jump Height(m)` and `Countermovement Depth(m)` are metres, `Time To Takeoff(s)` is seconds. CM depth arrives as a negative number, so it is mapped with `absolute: true` — without that, the `increase_bad` direction inverts and a deeper dip reads as improvement. All handled in `config.yaml` → `hawkin.metric_mapping`.
- **The Hawkin tests endpoint is the API root**, e.g. `https://cloud.hawkindynamics.com/api/v1?from=...`. There is no `/tests` path; requesting one returns 404.
- **Thresholds are vendor-specific.** `ecc_braking_rfd` and `countermovement_depth` were recalibrated for Hawkin in July 2026 because their original ForceDecks-tuned values sat below Hawkin's measurement noise floor. Do not copy thresholds between force-plate systems without checking them against measured trial-to-trial variability — see `docs/HAWKIN_API_INTEGRATION.md` §6.

## Configuration — No Code Changes Needed For

- Adjusting green/yellow/red thresholds: edit `thresholds.*.yellow_min` / `red_min`
- Changing recommendation language: edit `recommendations.*`
- Adding/removing athletes: edit `roster:`
- Changing ForceDecks column headers: edit `column_mapping:`

"""
build_share_package.py -- Zip the reports into a package a colleague can run.

The package holds only what the two reports need: the Hawkin fetch, both report
generators, templates and config. It leaves out email, tests, docs, and anything
private (.env, data/, output/). The colleague double-clicks "Run CMJ Report.bat";
see share/README.txt for what they see.

Usage:
    python scripts/build_share_package.py
    python scripts/build_share_package.py --out C:/Users/me/Desktop
"""

import argparse
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT_DIR   = Path(__file__).parent
PROJECT_ROOT = SCRIPT_DIR.parent
SHARE_DIR    = PROJECT_ROOT / "share"

PACKAGE_NAME = "CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report"

# run_pipeline imports import_data, so the legacy importer ships too.
SCRIPTS = [
    "fetch_hawkin.py",
    "generate_report.py",
    "generate_recovery_report.py",
    "run_pipeline.py",
    "import_data.py",
    "utils.py",
]

# Files cmd.exe or Notepad read; they need Windows line endings.
CRLF_SUFFIXES = {".bat", ".txt"}


def package_files() -> list[tuple[Path, str]]:
    """(source path, path inside the package) for every file shipped."""
    files = [(SCRIPT_DIR / name, f"scripts/{name}") for name in SCRIPTS]
    files.append((PROJECT_ROOT / "config" / "config.yaml", "config/config.yaml"))
    files += [(p, f"templates/{p.name}") for p in sorted((PROJECT_ROOT / "templates").glob("*.html"))]

entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- **Registry drift.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py crosswalk` (`portfolio_json` is in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`). It compares `portfolio.json` with every DEV folder and Drive `01_PROJECTS` folder and only reports; it never moves anything. Do not fix drift during closeout. List each item it found under "Still open", naming any folder created this session first: that is a project started without a row, the exact way projects got lost before the 2026-10-03 organization pass. `drive_unreachable` means the Drive checks never ran; say so, do not call it clean. Cowork cannot run it; say it was skipped.
- **7-day rule.** Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py seven-day --apply`. Name any project it paused, and any project on its last two days, under "Still open" with what it still needs (a receiver, step 1). Revive with the board's status pill or `portfolio.py` once there is a first step to show.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- **Registry edits get their own commit.** In project-triage, if `git status --porcelain portfolio.json` shows a change (board edits from the day, `set-status`, `set-receiver`), commit that file alone first as `data: board edits <YYYY-MM-DD>`, then the rest. The board header's "N unpushed registry edits" counts these; a skipped one becomes a JSON merge conflict when the other machine edits too.
- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- If `~/.claude/mods` changed this session (a mod added, edited or `.disabled`), run the mods sync (`bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh` on the Mac, `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\mods\mods-sync.ps1` on Windows) and list any invalid mod under "Still open".
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first. Item 1 is one concrete action (a command to run or a file to open), not a theme: it is the line `~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py` shows Eric the next morning
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric, each one written out in full as its own top-level bullet: the question itself and enough context to answer it without opening another file. Never a pointer ("See PLAN.md"): `/startup` reads this section across every repo with `where-was-i.py --decisions`, and a pointer gives no question to answer. Mark answered items `ANSWERED <date>: …` or strike them through (`~~…~~`) so they drop off that list. Leave the section empty, not "-", when nothing is waiting.
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

Then run `python ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 1`. It prints exactly what tomorrow's `/startup` will show as "Decisions waiting on you". Every decision this session left open must appear there as a readable question; if one is missing or shows as a pointer, fix that repo's `## Open questions` before the commit.

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

**Keep the resume cards true (PM system design Decision 9).** The live board shows each project as a card read from STATUS and the registry; if a card doesn't make sense tonight, it won't in six weeks. Run `python <dir of portfolio_json>/landed.py scan --days 1` (about a minute), then `python <dir of portfolio_json>/portfolio.py card-check`. It prints the card of every registry project touched today, on either machine, with its gaps. Fix each gap before the Step 2 commit:

- `STATUS has no entry dated <today>`: add `- <today>: <what happened>` under the repo's Done / Current state.
- `STATUS has no Next item`: put one concrete action first under `## Next`.
- `no next step (next_action)` (Drive-only row): set it on the board or with `portfolio.py add-update <name> "<note>" --next-action "<step>"`.
- `needs a receiver`: `portfolio.py set-receiver <name> "<who>"` (a name, or `me: <why>`). Ask Eric when it is not obvious from the session; never invent one.
- `touched but marked <status>`: revive it (`portfolio.py set-status <name> active`) or say in STATUS why a retired project was touched.

Re-run `card-check` after the fixes. Its output is the last section of the report (**Cards:**); trim to projects with work today if it is long, but never drop one that still has a gap.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Registry drift:** <N items, or "none"> (`portfolio.py crosswalk`)
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.

**Cards:** <`portfolio.py card-check` output, after the Step 4 fixes>
```

The cards come last on purpose: they are what the next session, on either machine, picks up from.

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

**Where everything landed.** Build that list from the ledger, not from memory: the Step 4 `landed.py scan --days 1` already refreshed it (it reads git in every DEV repo and file times on Drive and the vault, so files written by scripts and shell copies are included); run `landed.py show --days 1`. Put its project-grouped output in the report under **Landed:** (trim to the projects this session touched if it is long). The ledger lives in `~/.claude/global-memory/landed/` and is pushed with global-memory, so `/landed` on the other machine shows it too.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.
Running the closeout: a repo sweep first, then the registry checks, STATUS and handoff, the commits, and memory.

# 2026-10-05 — Shareable CMJ report package for Mike

## What and why
Eric wanted the volleyball CMJ traffic-light reports packaged so a colleague (Mike, Baylor staff cleared for the athlete data) can run them on his own Windows machine: unzip, double-click, reports land in `output\`.

## Decisions
- **Data source: Baylor's Hawkin account via Mike's own token.** Eric's token is never shipped. The launcher prompts for a token on first run and saves it to `.env` in the package folder.
- **Runtime: uv, downloaded on first run into `.tools\uv.exe`.** Mike has no Python; uv needs no admin rights and keeps Python and packages in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (out of synced folders). Run with `uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements requirements.txt`.
- **Both reports every run.** Fatigue report (`run_pipeline.py`) then recovery report, run unconditionally, since `run_pipeline.py` exits 0 when no session is paired.
- **First run backfills full history** (`fetch_hawkin.py --all`) when `data\master_data.csv` is missing, because the daily 14-day window is too short for the 6-session recovery report.
- **No Outlook step** in the colleague package; `pywin32` dropped from `share/requirements.txt`.
- **Roster ships in the zip.** Eric confirmed Mike is cleared. Auto-mode had blocked the build twice as data exfiltration before that.

## Files
- `share/Run CMJ Report.bat` — launcher (CRLF, ASCII)
- `share/README.txt` — colleague instructions
- `share/requirements.txt` — pandas, pyyaml, jinja2
- `scripts/build_share_package.py` — builds `CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report.zip` (default `dist/`, gitignored)
- `.gitignore` — adds `dist/`
- `docs/STATUS.md`
- Built zip: `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\CMJ_Traffic_Light_Report.zip` (not in git)
- Merged as PR #2 (`dd3238c`); branch deleted.

## Verification
- `pytest tests`: 87 passed.
- Clean extract, no token: uv downloaded, token prompt, clean exit.
- Clean extract with real token: backfill, fatigue report 2026-09-30 (12 paired: 7 green / 4 yellow / 1 red), recovery report (10 At Risk / 3 Watch / 4 Recovered), 42 s. Test copies deleted afterward.

## Next
1. Upload the zip to Drive, add the link to the email below, send to Mike.
2. First run with Mike.
3. Decide on Abby Schoene / Halle Bills (missing from roster).

## Email draft (not sent)

Subject: CMJ traffic light reports: run them on your machine

Mike,

Here's the volleyball CMJ report package: [Drive link]. One double-click gives you both reports: the post-practice fatigue report (pre vs post jumps, green/yellow/red per athlete) and the recovery report (pre-practice trend over the last 6 sessions).

Before the first run
1. Log in to Hawkin at cloud.hawkindynamics.com.
2. Go to Settings > Integrations and generate a refresh token. Copy it.

Running it
1. Download the zip and unzip it somewhere on your computer, such as Documents. Don't run it from inside the zip.
2. Open the folder and double-click "Run CMJ Report.bat".
3. If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click More info, then Run anyway.
4. When the window says the reports are ready, press any key to close it. Both reports open in your browser and are saved in the "output" folder.

The first run takes a few minutes. It downloads a small Python runner (nothing gets installed, no admin rights needed), asks you to paste your Hawkin token, and pulls the team's test history. After that, a run takes under a minute.

When to run it: after the post-practice jumps are uploaded to Hawkin. The fatigue report always covers the most recent session that has both pre and post jumps.

If something goes wrong
- A token error (401 or 403): delete the ".env" file in the folder and run it again to enter a new token.
- "No session has both pre and post tests": the post-practice jumps aren't in Hawkin yet. Run it again once they are.
- Anything else: send me a screenshot of the window.

Please don't pass on the ".env" file or the "data" folder. They hold your Hawkin login and athlete data.

Happy to sit with you for the first run.

Eric

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

CMJ Fatigue Traffic Light — a post-practice neuromuscular fatigue monitoring tool for Baylor Volleyball. It ingests ForceDecks countermovement jump (CMJ) CSV exports, pairs pre/post-practice tests per athlete, computes percent change on 6 biomechanical metrics, assigns traffic-light colors (green/yellow/red), and renders a self-contained HTML report. A separate recovery monitoring report tracks pre-practice CMJ trends across sessions to detect inter-session fatigue accumulation.

## Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Full pipeline (import CSVs + generate fatigue report for today)
python scripts/run_pipeline.py

# Full pipeline with overrides
python scripts/run_pipeline.py --date 2026-03-03 --session "Pre-Practice Assessment"

# Step-by-step (manual fallback)
```

- **Signal 1** — session-to-session delta: `calc_pct_change(prev_pre, current_pre)` vs config thresholds.

Cell indicators: `↓`/`↑` = moderate deviation from window average; `↓↓`/`↑↑` = large deviation. Direction matches metric direction (`decrease_bad` → `↓`/`↓↓`; `increase_bad` → `↑`/`↑↑`).

If no gap exceeds the threshold the session was a single bout and all trials are labelled `pre`.

Multiple trials per phase are reduced by `hawkin.trial_aggregation` (default `mean`).

- Adding/removing athletes: edit `roster:`
